statements.text: If you think about semiconductor export controls, there are only three countries that have toolmakers, the U.S., Japan, and the Netherlands. So if we could align on that it could be incredible.
statements.context: Senate Appropriations subcommittee hearing on the Commerce Department's FY2023 budget, where Secretary Raimondo responds to Senator Hagerty's questions about semiconductor policy and economic strategy in the Indo-Pacific.

statements.text: I very much appreciate the activity there at the Copyright Office of launching its new artificial intelligence initiative in March of this year. My hope is, Dr. Hayden, that you will continue to maintain your attention to this important matter.
statements.context: Senate hearing on Oversight of the Library of Congress, where Senator Hagerty questions the Librarian of Congress about the Copyright Office's AI initiative.

statements.text: I would like to talk with you about the United States Copyright Office. It is housed under the Library of Congress, and it has a unique role in ensuring the responsible implementation of new technologies such as artificial intelligence. [...] Tennessee is home to so many performing artists and songwriters who have the potential to be greatly impacted by artificial intelligence.
statements.context: Senate oversight hearing on the Library of Congress, where Senator Hagerty questions the Librarian of Congress about AI voice cloning and copyright protection.

statements.text: What I am concerned about is that Congress and the Biden Administration may be finding itself right at the same place again when we are looking at artificial intelligence, and I do not want to see us make the same set of mistakes. [...] I would like to start with a very basic question, if I might, and that is, is artificial intelligence a term with an agreed upon legal definition?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled "AI and the Future of Our Elections," Senator Hagerty questioning a witness.

statements.text: Is there a risk then, in your view, that hastily regulating in a very uncertain a rapidly growing concept like AI might actually chill political speech?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'AI and the Future of Our Elections' on September 27, 2023.

statements.text: What concerns me here is not just the collection, the storage, and the analysis of this highly sensitive data. It is also China's ability to use this trove of biological data and other life sciences data to train advanced dual-use artificial intelligence models, perhaps for malign purposes.
statements.context: Senate Banking Committee hearing on national security and emerging technology, Senator Hagerty questioning a witness about the national-security risks of Chinese company BGI's genomic data collection.

statements.text: One, the requirements for obtaining appropriate licenses or authorization to ingest or otherwise use materials that are copyrighted, or that implicate a person's rights of publicity or privacy. [...] Third, ensuring that appropriate transparency is maintained by AI companies.
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI use at the Library of Congress, GPO, and Smithsonian Institution.

statements.text: I am concerned that AI-generated deepfake recordings, voice clones, or other infringements on the works of copyright holders could cause serious damage to an artist's reputation and to their livelihood.
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI use at the Library of Congress, Government Publishing Office, and Smithsonian Institution.

statements.text: On a related matter, we, the United States, have worked with our allies to try to prevent the transfer of very high-end technologies to China in the first place, whether they be very high-end semiconductors, AI, or other technologies, and part of that strategy has been implemented through the Department of Commerce.
statements.context: Senate Appropriations subcommittee hearing on Financial Services and General Government appropriations for Fiscal Year 2025, with Treasury Secretary Yellen testifying.
